issues.t: Takata passenger airbag inflator (do-not-drive recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you can see or feel. The danger only shows up if the passenger airbag deploys in a crash.
issues.why: The passenger airbag inflator uses a propellant that breaks down with years of heat and humidity, so it can burst and throw metal pieces into the cabin. Ford told owners not to drive affected cars until the inflator is replaced, and later recalls also covered some replacement inflators.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open airbag recalls right away. If one is open, do not drive the car; ask the dealer to arrange the free repair and a tow if needed.

issues.t: Takata driver airbag inflator (recall)
issues.sym: No warning in normal driving. The risk appears only if the driver airbag deploys.
issues.why: The driver airbag inflator can also rupture after long exposure to heat and humidity. Ford recalled 2006-2011 Milans to replace it.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 21V-158 and get the free repair as soon as possible.

issues.t: ABS valves stick, brake pedal sinks farther
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels soft or sinks lower than normal before the car slows, stopping takes longer, or the brakes grab or lock unexpectedly.
issues.why: Valves inside the ABS hydraulic unit can react with some brake fluid additives and not close fully, so pedal travel grows. Soft brake pedals and grabbing brakes are the top Milan brake complaints, and Ford recalled 2006-2010 cars to flush the system and test or replace the unit.
issues.next: Have the brakes checked before normal driving. Check your VIN for recall 19V-904 and get the free repair.

issues.t: Driver floor mat can snag the gas pedal
issues.sym: The gas pedal sticks or does not return fully, especially with an all-weather mat in place.
issues.why: The driver all-weather floor mat can slide forward and catch the accelerator pedal. Ford recalled the mats.
issues.next: Remove any loose or stacked mats now and check your VIN for recall 14E-028. Use only a mat that is secured to the floor hooks.

issues.t: Sudden loss of power steering assist
issues.sym: The steering suddenly becomes very heavy, often with a power steering warning on the dash. Some owners say the steering felt locked up. It may come back after a restart and then fail again.
issues.why: The electric power steering rack and its motor sensor can fail and switch off the assist. It is the most-reported Milan problem. Ford recalled 2011 cars for a sensor fault, while 2010 owners mostly paid for new steering gears.
issues.next: You can still steer with extra effort, so slow down and pull over safely. Check your VIN for recall 15V-340 and have the system repaired before regular driving.

issues.t: Electronic throttle fault causes stalling or limp mode
issues.sym: A wrench light or check engine light comes on and the car suddenly loses power, holds a low engine speed, or stalls while driving.
issues.why: The electronic throttle body wears or builds up deposits, and the engine computer cuts power when the throttle readings don't agree. Throttle and stalling complaints are among the most common for the 2010 Milan.
issues.next: Have the codes read and drive gently to a shop. A cleaning or new throttle body usually fixes it; ask a dealer whether Ford's extended coverage on the throttle body applies to your VIN.

issues.t: Fuel tank can crack from EVAP purge valve fault (recall)
issues.sym: A gas smell, a check engine light, or trouble filling the tank.
issues.why: A faulty vapor canister purge valve can pull too much vacuum on the fuel tank, which can crack it and leak fuel. Ford recalled cars built from July 2008 to December 2010.
issues.next: A fuel smell is a fire risk; have it checked right away. Check your VIN for recall 15V-793.

issues.t: Wheel studs can break on 17-inch steel wheels (recall)
issues.sym: A clicking or clunking from a wheel, vibration, or a wheel that feels loose.
issues.why: Certain 17-inch steel wheels could let the wheel studs crack, and a wheel could come off. Ford recalled these cars to inspect and replace parts.
issues.next: Stop driving if a wheel feels loose or noisy. Check your VIN for recall 11V-574.

issues.t: Car may roll in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The car moves after being put in Park.
issues.why: A retention pin in the park mechanism may be missing, so Park may not hold. Ford recalled these cars.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake and check your VIN for recall 10V-222.

issues.t: Front seatback recliner may not hold in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No warning in normal use; the front seatback could move rearward in a crash.
issues.why: Gear teeth in the front manual seat recliner may be out of spec. Ford recalled these cars to inspect and replace recliners.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 10V-161.

issues.t: Rear LED brake or tail light fails
issues.sym: A brake or tail light that stays dark, stays on, or only lights a few LEDs. Owners report failed inspections and traffic stops.
issues.why: The rear LED lamp module fails, and it cannot be fixed with a bulb; the whole lamp must be replaced. Ford set up extended coverage for some 2010-2011 Milan tail lamps.
issues.next: Walk around the car with the brakes on to check. Ask a Lincoln or Ford dealer whether the extended coverage applies to your VIN before paying for a new lamp.

issues.t: Harsh shifts or automatic transmission failure
issues.sym: Harsh or jerky shifts, especially 1-2 and 3-4, shifting that gets worse over time, slipping, or the transmission failing completely.
issues.why: Owners of both four-cylinder and V6 cars report internal wear, torque converter debris and valve body faults. The wrong fluid makes it worse.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and type. If shifting is harsh or slipping, have it diagnosed early; a valve body repair is far cheaper than a rebuild.

issues.t: AWD power transfer unit leak or burnt fluid
issues.sym: A burning oil smell after driving, drips near the front of the car, or a whine from underneath.
issues.why: The power transfer unit that sends power to the rear wheels runs hot and holds little fluid. Its seals leak and the fluid breaks down, and there is no easy way to check the level.
issues.next: Have the unit inspected for leaks and the fluid changed. Fixing a seal early costs much less than replacing a failed unit.

issues.t: Interior door handle breaks
issues.sym: An inside door handle snaps, sticks open, or no longer opens the door.
issues.why: The plastic inside handles and their latch linkage crack. Owners of 2006 through 2010 Milans report broken handles, often on the driver door.
issues.next: Replace the broken handle. If a door won't open from inside, fix it soon in case you need to get out quickly.

issues.t: A/C drain clogs and floods the passenger floor
issues.sym: Water on the passenger-side floor, a wet carpet, or a musty smell after using the A/C.
issues.why: The A/C condensate drain plugs up, so water from the evaporator backs up into the cabin instead of dripping under the car.
issues.next: Have the drain tube cleared and the carpet dried quickly to prevent mold and damage to wiring under the floor.

issues.t: Knocking noise from the engine
issues.sym: A knock or tapping from the engine that gets louder over time, usually at high mileage.
issues.why: Owners report engine knocking on 2006 Milans, which can point to worn internal parts or low oil.
issues.next: Check the oil level right away. Have a mechanic find the source of the noise; driving on a deep knock can destroy the engine.

issues.t: Rough, flaring or delayed shifts
issues.sym: Harsh 1-2 or 2-3 shifts, the engine revving between gears, hesitation, or a clunk when the transmission shifts.
issues.why: The six-speed automatic in these years is sensitive to its software and fluid. Ford released computer updates and a service program, and some owners still needed internal clutch repairs. RepairPal lists harsh or delayed shifting as the most common Milan complaint.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check for transmission software updates for your VIN. If shifting stays rough or slips, have the fluid and internal parts checked before it fails.

issues.t: Thermostat sticks open, engine runs cold
issues.sym: The temperature gauge stays low, the heater blows lukewarm, or a check engine light comes on with a thermostat code.
issues.why: The thermostat on the 2.3L four-cylinder sticks open, so the engine never fully warms up. Owners report replacing it, sometimes along with the housing.
issues.next: Have the thermostat replaced. Running cold hurts fuel economy and heater output and keeps the check engine light on.

issues.t: Valve cover gasket leaks oil into spark plug wells
issues.sym: A burning oil smell, oil on the top of the engine, or a misfire and check engine light.
issues.why: The valve cover gasket on the 2.3L hardens and leaks, and oil can run down into the spark plug wells and damage the coils.
issues.next: Have the gasket and plug well seals replaced before oil ruins the ignition coils.

issues.t: Check engine light from secondary air injection valve
issues.sym: A check engine light with secondary air system codes; the car usually drives normally.
issues.why: The secondary air injection system pumps air into the exhaust on cold starts to cut emissions. Its control or check valve fails on the 2.3L four-cylinder.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Replace the failed valve so the car can pass an emissions test.

issues.t: Broken engine or transmission mounts
issues.sym: A thump or clunk when shifting into gear or accelerating, and more vibration at idle.
issues.why: Owners report broken or worn engine and transmission mounts on both the four-cylinder and V6, sometimes letting the engine move noticeably.
issues.next: Have the mounts inspected and replace any that are cracked or collapsed.

issues.t: Serpentine belt tensioner or pulley wears
issues.sym: A squeal or chirp from the front of the engine, especially on cold starts, or a belt that slips or comes off.
issues.why: The drive belt tensioner and idler pulleys wear out; owners of several years report replacing the belt and tensioner.
issues.next: Replace a worn tensioner along with the belt. A belt that comes off can stop the alternator and water pump.

issues.t: Blower motor or resistor fails
issues.sym: The fan only works on some speeds, stops working, chirps or clicks, or there is a burning smell from the dash.
issues.why: Owners report failed blower motors, blower resistors and blower wiring connectors.
issues.next: Have the blower circuit checked. If there is a burning smell, have the connector inspected too, since a melted connector will ruin a new motor.

issues.t: Worn tie rods, ball joints and control arm bushings
issues.sym: Clunks or creaks over bumps and while turning, loose steering, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: Tie rod ends, ball joints, control arm bushings and sway bar links wear on these cars. RepairPal lists squeaks and creaks over bumps and while turning among common Milan complaints.
issues.next: Have the front end checked for play and get an alignment after replacing parts.

issues.t: Wheel bearing grinding or groaning
issues.sym: A hum, groan or grinding noise that grows with speed.
issues.why: Owners report front and rear wheel bearings wearing out, including on hybrid and AWD models.
issues.next: Have the noisy corner found and the bearing or hub replaced before it gets loose.

issues.t: Rear brake calipers stick
issues.sym: The car pulls or drags, a hot or burning smell from a rear wheel, or rear pads that wear out unevenly.
issues.why: Owners report rear calipers seizing, sometimes right after a pad and rotor job.
issues.next: Have the calipers and slide pins checked. A stuck caliper wears pads fast and can overheat the brakes.

issues.t: Check engine light from capless fuel filler or EVAP leak
issues.sym: A check engine light with a small evaporative leak code, often after refueling.
issues.why: The capless fuel filler valve can fail to seal fully, and the EVAP purge valve can stick. Owners report both on 2010-2011 cars.
issues.next: Make sure the fuel nozzle was inserted fully and the filler is clean. If the light stays on, have the EVAP system smoke-tested; also check that the purge valve recall has been done.

issues.t: Airbag light or steering wheel buttons fail (clockspring)
issues.sym: The airbag light comes on, or the steering wheel audio and phone buttons stop working.
issues.why: The clockspring, a coiled ribbon cable behind the steering wheel, wears and breaks the connection to the airbag and wheel controls.
issues.next: Have the airbag codes read. The driver airbag may not work while the light is on.

issues.t: Hybrid wrench light or dead 12-volt battery
issues.sym: A wrench light or hybrid warning, or the car won't power up because the small 12-volt battery is flat.
issues.why: Owners of the Milan Hybrid report wrench lights fixed by updating out-of-date engine computer software, and 12-volt battery failures. The hybrid still needs its 12-volt battery to start.
issues.next: Have the 12-volt battery tested first. For a wrench light, ask a dealer about software updates for your VIN.
